title: Derivative of a function at a point
competency: Use the definition to find the derivative of a function at a point.

keywords.def: f′(a): the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).
Having a derivative: the difference quotient settles at one value from both sides.

en.text: The derivative f′(a) is the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)). It is what (f(a + h) − f(a))/h approaches as h gets closer to 0 from both sides. If it exists, f is differentiable at a.

am.text: f′(a) በ (a, f(a)) ላይ ያለው የታንጀንቱ ግራዲየንት ነው፤ h ከሁለቱም አቅጣጫ ወደ 0 ሲቀርብ (f(a + h) − f(a))/h የሚቀርበው ቁጥር።

screens.title: A name for the gradient
screens.ask: For f(x) = x² + 3, (f(5 + h) − f(5))/h = h + 10. As h → 0 this becomes
screens.after:
(f(5 + h) − f(5))/h = h + 10.
As h → 0, h + 10 → 10.
This number is the derivative of f at 5, written f′(5) = 10.
28 is f(5), a y-value, not a gradient.

screens.title: Derivative at a point
paras: f′(a) is the gradient of the tangent line to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).
As h gets closer to zero from both directions, (f(a + h) − f(a))/h becomes closer to f′(a).
If f′(a) exists, f is differentiable at a.

screens.title: From both sides
screens.ask: f(x) = x² + 3 at a = 5. The quotient is h + 10. Tap each h.
items: From the right and from the left the values settle at 10. So f′(5) = 10 and f is differentiable at 5.

screens.title: Key words
defs: f′(a): the gradient of the tangent to y = f(x) at (a, f(a)).
Having a derivative: the difference quotient settles at one value from both sides.

screens.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = 5x − 3 at x = −2: f′(−2) = ___
screens.why:
f(−2) = −10 − 3 = −13.
f(−2 + h) = 5(−2 + h) − 3 = −13 + 5h.
Difference: 5h. Divide by h: 5.
The limit as h → 0 is 5.
A line's derivative is its slope, at every point.
screens.clue: A straight line has the same gradient everywhere.

screens.title: Quotient and derivative of x² + 3
screens.note: Move h towards 0 from either side. The quotient 2a + h settles at f′(a) = 2a.

screens.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = 9x − 7 at x = 2: f′(2) = ___
screens.why:
f(2) = 18 − 7 = 11.
f(2 + h) − f(2) = 9(2 + h) − 7 − 11 = 9h.
Divide by h: 9.
So f′(2) = 9, the slope of the line.

screens.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = x² − 1 at x = 2: f′(2) = ___
screens.why:
f(2 + h) = 4 + 4h + h² − 1 = 3 + 4h + h².
f(2) = 3.
Difference: 4h + h². Divide by h: 4 + h.
As h → 0: f′(2) = 4.

screens.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = x³ + 2x at x = 3: f′(3) = ___
screens.why:
f(3) = 27 + 6 = 33.
f(3 + h) = 27 + 27h + 9h² + h³ + 6 + 2h.
Difference: 29h + 9h² + h³.
Divide by h: 29 + 9h + h².
As h → 0: f′(3) = 29.

screens.text: Find the derivative of f(x) = √(3x − 6) at x = 3: f′(3) =
screens.why:
f(3) = √3 and f(3 + h) = √(3 + 3h).
Multiply by the conjugate: the top becomes (3 + 3h) − 3 = 3h.
Cancel h: 3/(√(3 + 3h) + √3).
As h → 0: 3/(2√3) = 3√3/6 = √3/2.
Trap: 3/2 forgets the roots in the bottom.

The quotient is already simplified: no 0/0 is left.
Let x approach 1: −(1 + 1)/1² = −2.
So f′(1) = −2. The curve falls at x = 1.

screens.ask: Find the missing number: f(x) = x² + kx and f′(1) = 7. k = ___
screens.why:
f(1 + h) − f(1) = (1 + 2h + h²) + k + kh − 1 − k = 2h + h² + kh.
Divide by h: 2 + h + k.
As h → 0: f′(1) = 2 + k.
2 + k = 7, so k = 5.
Check: x² + 5x gives f′(1) = 2 + 5 = 7. ✓
screens.clue: Find f′(1) in terms of k.

items.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = 9x − 7 at a = 2: f′(2) = ___
items.why:
f(2 + h) − f(2) = 9h.
Divide by h: 9.
f′(2) = 9.

items.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = x² − 1 at a = 2: f′(2) = ___
items.why:
f(2 + h) − f(2) = 4h + h².
Divide by h: 4 + h.
As h → 0: f′(2) = 4.

items.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = x³ + 2x at a = 3: f′(3) = ___
items.why:
f(3 + h) − f(3) = 29h + 9h² + h³.
Divide by h: 29 + 9h + h².
As h → 0: f′(3) = 29.

items.text: Find the derivative of f(x) = √(3x − 6) at a = 3: f′(3) =
items.why:
Rationalise: (√(3 + 3h) − √3)/h = 3/(√(3 + 3h) + √3).
As h → 0: 3/(2√3).
Multiply top and bottom by √3: 3√3/6 = √3/2.

test.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x + 1 at x = 7: f′(7) = ___
test.why:
f(7) = 29. f(7 + h) − f(7) = 4(7 + h) + 1 − 29 = 4h.
Divide by h: 4.
A line's derivative is its slope, 4, everywhere.

test.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = x² + 2 at x = 3: f′(3) = ___
test.why:
f(3 + h) = 9 + 6h + h² + 2 and f(3) = 11.
Difference: 6h + h². Divide by h: 6 + h.
As h → 0: f′(3) = 6.

test.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = 2x² at x = −1: f′(−1) = ___
test.why:
f(−1 + h) = 2(1 − 2h + h²) = 2 − 4h + 2h².
f(−1) = 2.
Difference: −4h + 2h². Divide by h: −4 + 2h.
As h → 0: f′(−1) = −4.

test.ask: Find the derivative of f(x) = √x at x = 9: f′(9) = ___
Find the derivative of f(x) = x³ at x = −2: f′(−2) = ___
test.why:
(−2 + h)³ = −8 + 12h − 6h² + h³ and f(−2) = −8.
Difference: 12h − 6h² + h³. Divide by h: 12 − 6h + h².
As h → 0: f′(−2) = 12.
Trap: −12. The gradient 3a² is never negative.

notes.text: p.80 Note: "If y = f′(x) is defined" should read "If f′(a) exists, f is differentiable at a".
